title: India 🇮🇳 vs Pakistan 🇵🇰: 20 rounds, real data. Who wins?
headline: India or *Pakistan*?
description: India against Pakistan in 20 rounds: people, money, army, the rupee and daily life, plus a quiz where you play along. Every number is real World Bank data. India or Pakistan? Comment your flag.
source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (latest year with data for both countries per round, 2020-2025), data.worldbank.org

segments.text: India against Pakistan. Twenty rounds. Real numbers. Keep score.
Pakistan wins rounds you would never guess. And one chapter ends four to zero.
First up. People. Who has the bigger crowd?
Population. India has almost six times more people.
Population growth. Pakistan grows almost twice as fast.
Life in cities. Pakistan wins again. Almost forty percent live in a city.
Life expectancy. People in India live four years longer.
The people chapter ends in a draw. Two all.
No points for this one. Just watch the biggest countries on earth since 1990.
In 1990, Pakistan is not even in the top six.
Then it climbs. In 1999, Pakistan passes Russia.
In 2009, it passes Brazil.
And in 2021, India passes China. Now it has more people than any country on earth.
Pakistan has more than doubled since 1990. India grew by almost seventy percent.
Next up. Money. The score is two all.
Size of the economy. India's economy is almost ten times bigger.
Income per person. India leads by almost seventy percent.
But it was not always like this. In 2005, Pakistan was richer per person. India passed it for good in 2009.
Now a twist. How much the average person spends in a year. Pakistan wins.
The reason? India saves thirty-five percent of its income. Pakistan saves fifteen.
Reserves and gold. India holds more than twenty-six times as much.
Exports. India sells almost twenty-two times more to the world.
India takes the money chapter. Four to one. Overall, six to three.
Your turn. Three rounds. Guess before the timer ends. These count too. Who has more people online?
India. Sixty-five percent against fifty-seven.
Round two. Who uses more electricity per person?
India. Two and a half times more.
Last one. Where do fewer young people struggle to find a job?
Pakistan. About ten percent. In India, it is sixteen.
How many did you get? The score is now eight to four.
Now the army. Only numbers. No politics.
Soldiers. India has more than three times as many.
Military budget. India spends almost eight times more.
But as a share of the economy, Pakistan spends more. Almost three percent.
Two to one for India. Overall, ten to five.
Both countries call their money the rupee. In 1990, one dollar bought twenty-two Pakistani rupees. Guess what it buys now.
Two hundred eighty-one. Almost thirteen times more.
In 1990, one dollar bought seventeen and a half Indian rupees.
Today, eighty-seven. Five times more. The Indian rupee held on better. Point to India. Eleven to five.
Last chapter. Daily life. Four rounds left.
Prices. They rise slower in India.
Jobs. Fewer people are out of work in India.
Mobile phones per hundred people. India wins. But only just.
Women at work. Almost one in three in India. One in four in Pakistan.
There it is. Four to zero for India.
Final score. India fifteen. Pakistan five.
Pakistan took five rounds. It is younger. It grows faster. And its people spend more.
India or Pakistan? Comment your flag.
